endorsements.name: Jesson Soto Ventura
endorsements.label: CVE-2025-24002
endorsements.description: An unauthenticated remote attacker can use MQTT messages to crash a service on charging stations complying with German Calibration Law, resulting in a temporary denial-of-service for these stations until they got restarted by the watchdog.
endorsements.subtitle: CVE · Severity: MEDIUM (CVSS 3.1, 5.3)

povs.explanation: A published CVE record provides public, independently verifiable recognition of the credited vulnerability disclosure.

endorsements.name: Jesson Soto Ventura
endorsements.label: CVE-2025-24003
endorsements.description: An unauthenticated remote attacker can use MQTT messages to trigger out-of-bounds writes in charging stations complying with German Calibration Law, resulting in a loss of integrity for only EichrechtAgents and potential denial-of-service for these stations.
endorsements.subtitle: CVE · Severity: HIGH (CVSS 3.1, 8.2)

povs.explanation: A published CVE record provides public, independently verifiable recognition of the credited vulnerability disclosure.

endorsements.name: Jesson Soto Ventura
endorsements.label: CVE-2025-24004
endorsements.description: A physical attacker with access to the device display via USB-C can send a message to the device which triggers an unsecure copy to a buffer resulting in loss of integrity and a temporary denial-of-service for the stations until they got restarted by the watchdog.
endorsements.subtitle: CVE · Severity: MEDIUM (CVSS 3.1, 5.2)
